text:
Sylvia: FYI — new zeus11b int4 canary went live this morning. Stressbench + some production smoke shows intermittent OOMs on p4d workers. Repro ~4% on long chat flows (>600 tokens) when batch_size >= 3. Suspect memory fragmentation + KV growth.

Carlos: Ugh. Did you see if it's happening during prefix-heavy workloads or mostly long generations?

Sylvia: Mostly long gens. Prefix size doesn't seem correlated. Logs show allocations failing during decoding: `cudaMalloc` fails even though free memory reported ~7GB — allocation request ~8GB. Feels like fragmentation.

Ben: Can confirm stack traces: `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 8589934592 bytes` followed by a bunch of kernel launches. Happens after ~250 tokens into gen when kv cache grows.

Ryan: Quick mitigation we tried in a test pool: lowered default max_new_tokens from 512 -> 256, and capped per-request batch_size to 2. Also turned on slot_compactor and reduced async pool to 1G. OOMs dropped to ~1.2%.

Carlos: Config snippet we used: `{"defaults": {"max_new_tokens": 256, "batching": {"max_batch": 2, "queue_ms": 10}, "kv_trim": {"enabled": true, "threshold": 0.65, "trim_step": 32}}}`

Sophia: Note — when we compressed attention weights to int4 we observed a small quality delta on summarization evals (ROUGE -0.6). If we constrain some attention layers to int8 (or fp16), quality recovers. Might be worth hybrid quantization instead of full int4.

Ben: Agreed. Short-term: prefer operational mitigations (batch/max_new_tokens/kv_trim). Medium-term: run a per-layer quant sweep: attention & output projection at int8, rest int4. Also investigate allocator: async pool sizing + compaction frequency.

Sylvia: I'm going to roll 256 + batch=2 + kv_trim to 10% traffic on the canary for 6h. If stable, expand and then run a quant-sensitivity eval across the eval suite (QA, summarization, chat).

Infra-bot: Canary config updated by @carlos at 7312345680 :white_check_mark: New defaults applied to zeus11b-int4-canary.

Ryan: One more thing — we saw memory churn correlates with concurrent short-lived sessions. Adding prefix cache TTL and aggressive kv-eviction for sessions > 400 tokens helped in test. Suggest adding a heuristic: if session_len + expected_gen > 700, force batch=1 and kv_trim.

Sophia: For the eval plan: run mixed-precision sweep + throughput bench with max_batch 1/2/3, max_new_tokens 128/256/512. Capture latency p95, OOM rate, and metric deltas.

Carlos: I'll open a small automation to run those combos on a 5-node canary slice tomorrow.

Sylvia: Thanks — will monitor and paste telemetry after 6h. If OOMs persist we'll fallback to a temporary routing policy sending heavy chats to a larger instance type until we ship allocator fixes. :thumbsup:
